description: Route-tree classification spec: templates + rule thresholds. Source of truth for route_hybrid.py - edit this file, not the code.

conventions.frame: Receiver-relative. Origin (0,0) is the receiver's position at the snap.
conventions.depth: +depth = yards downfield past the line of scrimmage.
conventions.inside: +inside = yards toward the middle of the field; -inside = toward his nearest sideline. Derived from which half of the field he lined up on, so a slant and a quick-out are not mirror images.

matching.gamma_note: Weight on the template->route distance term. Total = mean(route->template) + gamma * mean(template->route). Two-way per Kinney (arXiv:2003.05428), so a template that overlaps only part of a route cannot win.
matching.scale_note: Scaling is uniform in both axes so break ANGLES never distort - angles are what separate routes. Templates in a depth ladder (same break direction, different depth) get tight bands or they collapse into each other.
matching.other_note: Above this match_dist (yd), the nearest template is still a bad fit, not a real match - relabel OTHER rather than report a confident-looking wrong name. Checked at 2024-09: ~7.9% of routes land here (option routes with an actual loop, and other shapes no template family fits well). Chasing this tail with more templates hits diminishing returns fast - going from DRAG's original 42.7%-of-SLANT problem to this was already a ~200x drop in scale.

FLAT (1).note: shallow, to the sideline. Ladder with OUT (5).

SLANT (2).note: immediate 45 deg inside. Ladder with DIG (6).

DRAG.note: Not in the numbered tree. Added because 42.7% of routes matched to SLANT were actually flat crossers (18.8 yds lateral at 6.8 yds depth).

FADE.note: Not in the numbered tree. Added because 28.6% of CORNERs were the corner template stretched >=1.8x to cover gradual deep drift.

CROSS.note: Not in the numbered tree. Added because 24.7% of routes matched to DRAG had match_dist > 5yd and a genuinely steeper angle (~24 deg vs DRAG's ~14 deg) that got worse the deeper they went - not a scale problem, a different shape. Median of that population's own shape, not a guess.

SEAM.note: Not in the numbered tree. Added from k-means clustering of the OTHER bucket: 37% of it (2.9% of all routes) was one tight cluster with a near-identical overall angle to CROSS (~24 deg) but a STRAIGHT diagonal from the snap, not CROSS's curve (CROSS's midpoint sits well below the straight line start-to-end; this cluster's midpoint sits right on it) - a constant-angle deep diagonal with no vertical stem, unlike CORNER/POST which run straight for 12yd first.

rules.note: Evaluated in this order, first match wins; anything reaching the end goes to template matching. These five cannot be templated - see why_not_templated.

SCREEN.label: SCREEN
SCREEN.why_not_templated: Defined by the ABSENCE of movement, not by a shape. No polyline to match against.

ANGLE.label: ANGLE
ANGLE.why_not_templated: Dips behind the LOS before releasing upfield (a backfield hook-and-go), so like the reversal family its own outbound and return legs overlap - point-to-polyline distance can't see the dip, only the net shape after it. 24.7% of DRAG's worst fits (match_dist > 5yd) were this shape, not a deep crosser.

WHEEL.label: WHEEL
WHEEL.condition: shallow_outside >= wheel_min_outside AND climb_after >= wheel_min_climb AND net_inside <= wheel_max_net_inside AND abs(final_heading) <= wheel_max_final_heading
WHEEL.why_not_templated: Two-phase (flat to the sideline, THEN vertical up it). A single scaled polyline expresses it poorly, and a loose version swallowed every deep fade - it was 7.5% of routes before being tightened to 2.5%.

REVERSAL_FAMILY.why_not_templated: A doubling-back route lays its return path on top of its outbound path, so point-to-polyline distance is blind to the reversal. Kinney (arXiv:2003.05428) predicted ZERO curls and comebacks for exactly this reason and left it to future work; handling them by rule is where this beats the paper.

backfield_rb.condition: position in [RB, FB, HB] AND abs(start_x) < 4.0
backfield_rb.note: Kinney excludes backfield running backs: they navigate the offensive and defensive lines rather than running the route tree. Flagged in the output rather than dropped.

artifact_filters.note: Chart-scraping artifacts in route_coords.csv. Not applied by the classifier - filter upstream if you want clean input.

start_downfield.note: Physically impossible - a route starts at the LOS. Already flagged by the scraper's own start_ok column (catches 100% of these).

label_glyph.condition: bbox < 6yd AND closed loop < 2.5yd AND abs(centre_x) >= 24
label_glyph.note: The bowl of the 'O' in the chart's LOS/yard labels, traced as a route. Fixed upstream in next_gen_scrapy calib.text_mask + routes.is_label_glyph.

references: Kinney, M. (2020). Template Matching Route Classification. arXiv:2003.05428
